handRanking.title: Hand Ranking Blitz
handRanking.subtitle: Quickly identify the 9 hand rankings and compare two hands
handRanking.identifyPrompt: Identify the hand rank of these 5 cards:

q1.explanation: Hand B is AKQJT suited (Royal Flush), the strongest hand in Texas Hold'em, beating the plain AKQJT straight.

q2.explanation: Hand B is AAKKK full house (trip Kings + pair Aces), which beats trip 9s.

q3.explanation: Hand A is a flush (5 hearts), Hand B is a straight. Flush > Straight.

q4.explanation: AKQJT all spades — Royal Flush, the strongest hand in Texas Hold'em.

q5.explanation: 98765 all hearts — Straight Flush (not royal, since not AKQJT).

q6.explanation: KKK99 is trip Kings + pair 9s = Full House. Don't confuse with two pair or trips.

q7.explanation: T9876 is 5 consecutive cards = Straight (note: not all same suit).

q8.explanation: AAAQ2 is Three of a Kind Aces (three same rank + two kickers).

q9.explanation: AA is the strongest starting hand, far stronger than 22. Higher pocket pair wins.

q10.explanation: AKs (suited AK) is a strong starting hand, far better than 72o (offsuit 72), one of the weakest.

position.title: Position Awareness
position.subtitle: Identify positions on a 6-max table and understand position advantage

q1.prompt: Which position acts last preflop and is considered the best? (Dealer)
q1.explanation: BTN (Button) acts last preflop, giving the most information before deciding.

q2.explanation: UTG (Under The Gun) acts first preflop with the least information — play only strong hands.

q3.prompt: Which position acts last both preflop and postflop, called the 'best position'?
q3.explanation: BTN acts last both preflop and postflop — the most profitable position at the table.

q4.prompt: In 6-max, the position to the left of the button (posts small blind) is?
q4.explanation: SB (Small Blind) sits left of BTN, posts 0.5BB forced bet, out of position postflop.

q5.prompt: Which position posts the big blind?
q5.explanation: BB (Big Blind) sits left of SB, posts 1BB forced bet, last blind to act preflop.

q6.prompt: After a UTG raise preflop, which blind position acts last (closes action)?
q6.explanation: BB is the last to act preflop (among blinds), closing action — a positional advantage.

q7.prompt: From which position should you raise to steal blinds most often?
q7.explanation: BTN is the best steal position — only SB and BB left to act, high success rate.

q8.prompt: In 6-max, the position immediately after UTG is?
q8.explanation: MP (Middle Position) follows UTG, slightly better than UTG but still requires tight ranges.

outs.title: Outs Calculation Drill
outs.subtitle: Identify drawing hands and quickly count Outs, master the Rule of 2 and 4
outs.rulePrompt: Calculate your current number of Outs

q1.prompt: You hold suited AK, flop shows 2 of your suit. How many Outs?
q1.explanation: Flush draw: 13 suited cards - 4 visible = 9 outs.

q2.prompt: You hold suited 89, flop has 2 of your suit. How many Outs?
q2.explanation: Flush draw = 9 outs (13-4=9), the most common strong draw.

q3.prompt: You hold 89, board is 7T2. How many Outs for your OESD (open-ended straight draw)?
q3.explanation: OESD: any 6 or J completes the straight = 8 outs.

q4.prompt: You hold 56, board is 479. How many Outs for your OESD?
q4.explanation: OESD: any 3 or 8 completes the straight = 8 outs.

q5.prompt: You hold 79, board is 56K. How many Outs for your Gutshot?
q5.explanation: Gutshot (inside straight): only an 8 completes = 4 outs.

q6.prompt: You hold TJ, board is 792. How many Outs for your Gutshot?

q7.prompt: 8 Outs from turn→river equals approximately what equity? (Rule of 2 and 4)
q7.explanation: Rule of 2: 8 outs × 2 ≈ 16% equity (turn→river single street).

q8.prompt: You hold AK high, board has no A or K. How many Outs to hit top pair?
q8.explanation: AK high drawing to top pair: 3 Aces + 3 Kings = 6 outs.

overview.title: Platform Overview
overview.intro: Understand the platform layout and learning path
overview.s0: This platform is a pure front-end poker training tool with 8 functional modules: Range Trainer, Pot Odds Calculator, GTO Simulator, Strategy Academy, Theory Academy, Puzzle Trainer, Hand History, and Progress Tracking. All data is stored locally in your browser — no registration required.

s1-steps.0: Complete the placement test to get a personalized starting point
s1-steps.1: Enter Strategy Academy and start with L1 basics
s1-steps.2: Complete quick drills and daily puzzles every day to stay sharp
s1-steps.3: Check progress stats regularly to identify and work on weak areas

overview.s2: Tip: You don't need to use all modules in a fixed order. Choose your starting point based on your level, focus on weaknesses, and maintain strengths.

range-trainer.title: Range Trainer
range-trainer.intro: Learn and quiz starting hand ranges by position
range-trainer.s0: Range Trainer helps you memorize and understand opening ranges for each position. The 13×13 matrix visualization shows exactly which hands to open, call, or 3-bet from each seat.

s1-steps.0: Use Learn mode to browse standard range charts for each position
s1-steps.1: Switch to Quiz mode for randomized questions testing your memory
s1-steps.2: Review feedback to correct mistakes, focusing on frequently missed positions
s1-steps.3: Unlock more positions as your ELO rises (UTG → HJ → CO → BTN → SB → BB)

range-trainer.s2: Common mistake: Don't try to memorize all positions at once. Start with BTN and CO — they have the widest ranges and appear most frequently.

pot-odds.title: Pot Odds Calculator
pot-odds.intro: Master pot odds and equity calculations
pot-odds.s0: The Pot Odds Calculator helps you quickly determine if a call is +EV. Input the pot size, opponent's bet, and your outs count to see whether you should continue.

s1-steps.0: Enter the current pot size and opponent's bet amount
s1-steps.1: Estimate your outs — the system calculates equity automatically
s1-steps.2: Enter Quiz mode for timed questions to build calculation speed

pot-odds.s2: Common mistake: Don't double-count outs. For example, a flush draw has 9 outs — don't add straight draw outs on top (they may overlap).

gto-simulator.title: GTO Simulator
gto-simulator.intro: Practice GTO decisions in simulated scenarios
gto-simulator.s0: The GTO Simulator provides pre-computed game theory optimal strategy scenarios. You make decisions on specific boards and positions, and the system compares your choice against the GTO solution with EV loss feedback.

s1-steps.1: Read the scenario description and make your decision (fold/call/raise)
s1-steps.2: Review the GTO optimal solution and EV difference from your choice
s1-steps.3: Focus on wrong/blunder level feedback and review related lessons

gto-simulator.s2: Common mistake: GTO isn't the only correct strategy. Against specific opponent types, exploitative play may be more profitable. GTO training builds a baseline thinking framework.

academy.title: Strategy Academy
academy.s0: Strategy Academy offers an 8-level curriculum from beginner to advanced. Each level includes video-style lessons, concept graphs, and drill exercises. Pass certification exams to unlock the next level.

s1-steps.0: Start from L1 and study each level's content in order
s1-steps.1: Complete post-lesson drills to reinforce what you've learned
s1-steps.2: Pass the level certification exam (≥70% accuracy) to unlock the next level
s1-steps.3: Use Quick Drill mode to randomly review previously learned material

academy.s2: Common mistake: Don't skip drills and go straight to exams. The instant feedback from drills helps you truly understand concepts rather than just memorize.

theory.title: Theory Academy
theory.s0: Theory Academy provides systematic poker theory learning, from probability basics to advanced game theory. Parallel to Strategy Academy, forming a 'theory → practice' loop.

s1-steps.0: Start from T1 Probability and unlock 9 levels sequentially
s1-steps.1: Each chapter includes concept explanations + end-of-chapter quizzes with automatic progress tracking
s1-steps.2: Follow 'Practice Bridge' cards to connect theory with Strategy Academy lessons

theory.s2: Common mistake: Theory study can't replace practice. After completing each theory level, do exercises in the corresponding module (e.g., odds quizzes after learning odds theory).

puzzle.title: Poker Puzzles
puzzle.intro: Three modes to train decision intuition
puzzle.s0: Puzzle Trainer offers three modes: Rush (timed consecutive questions), Daily Puzzle (one question per day, same for all players), and Theme Drill (topic-specific practice).

s1-steps.0: Daily Puzzle: one question per day, compete with players worldwide
s1-steps.1: Rush: answer as many as possible in 60 seconds, chase your best record
s1-steps.2: Theme Drill: select specific themes (e.g., RFI, 3-bet) for focused practice
s1-steps.3: Track your consecutive correct streak to maintain momentum

puzzle.s2: Common mistake: Don't sacrifice accuracy for speed. Make sure you understand the logic of each question first, then gradually increase pace.

hand-history.title: Hand History
hand-history.intro: Import and analyze your real-game hands
hand-history.s0: Hand History supports importing from PokerStars, GGPoker, and PartyPoker formats. The system auto-parses and provides GTO deviation analysis.

s1-steps.0: Export hand history files (.txt) from your poker platform
s1-steps.1: Paste or upload files on the import page — format is auto-detected
s1-steps.2: Review parsed results and click any hand to enter replay mode
s1-steps.3: Check the GTO deviation panel to identify decision mistakes

hand-history.s2: Common mistake: Don't only review big pots you lost. Frequent small mistakes accumulate to a larger impact — review comprehensively.

progress.title: Progress Tracking
progress.intro: Track your training data and growth trajectory
progress.s0: Progress Tracking aggregates data from all modules, including ELO ratings, training streaks, accuracy trends, weakness analysis, and other visualizations.

s1-steps.0: View the dashboard overview: today's volume, ELO changes, streak count
s1-steps.1: Enter detailed stats pages to see per-module accuracy trends
s1-steps.2: Check weakness analysis — the system recommends areas needing improvement

progress.s2: Tip: Daily consistent training is more effective than occasional marathon sessions. The system tracks your streak — ELO decays if you stop.

concepts.title: System Concepts
concepts.subtitle: Brief explanations of the six core systems

elo.title: ELO Rating System
elo.body: Each training module has an independent ELO score. Correct answers add points, wrong answers subtract — harder questions cause larger swings. Ranks range from 'Novice' to 'Grandmaster' across 8 tiers.

streak.title: Streak & Freeze Cards
streak.body: Your training streak tracks learning consistency. Missing a day resets it to zero. Freeze cards protect one day without training — earn them by maintaining a 7-day streak.

srs.title: SRS Spaced Repetition
srs.body: Based on the SM-2 algorithm. Missed questions are automatically added to a review queue, reminding you to review at optimal intervals for long-term retention.

feedback.title: Five-Level Feedback
feedback.body: Each answer receives a grade based on EV loss: best (optimal) / correct / inaccuracy / wrong / blunder (critical mistake).

sessionLimit.title: Daily Question Limit
sessionLimit.body: Configure a daily training cap in Settings. When reached, the system suggests a break to prevent fatigue-driven diminishing returns. Set to 0 for unlimited.

dataStorage.title: Data Storage & Export
dataStorage.body: All data is stored in browser localStorage. Export a JSON backup from Settings, and import it on a new device. Clearing browser data will erase your records.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Common questions about data, language, offline, freeze cards

q0.question: Where is my data stored?
q0.answer: All training data is stored in your browser's localStorage and is never uploaded to any server. Clearing browser data or switching browsers will cause data loss — export backups regularly from Settings.

q1.question: How do I migrate data to a new device?
q1.answer: Click 'Export Data' in Settings on your old device to download a JSON file, then click 'Import Data' on the new device and select that file to restore all training records.

q2.question: Does it work offline?
q2.answer: Yes. This is a PWA app — after the first load, all features work offline. In supported browsers, you can 'Add to Home Screen' for an app-like experience.

q3.question: How do I switch languages?
q3.answer: Three ways: the language toggle in the top bar, the language button at the bottom of the sidebar, or the language dropdown in Settings. Changes apply immediately and preferences are saved automatically.

q4.question: How do I get and use freeze cards?
q4.answer: Maintain a 7-day training streak to automatically earn 1 freeze card. When you can't train one day, click 'Use Freeze Card' in Settings to protect your streak. Maximum 1 per day.

q5.question: What happens if my streak breaks?
q5.answer: Your streak resets to 0. ELO scores don't reset but will decay slightly. After a break, start with easier questions to rebuild momentum.

q6.question: What is debug unlock?
q6.answer: Debug unlock in Developer Options bypasses all learning progress gates (course levels, position unlocks, daily limits, etc.). It's for development testing only — regular users don't need it.

q7.question: Can I recover data after clearing?
q7.answer: No. The 'Clear All Data' action in Settings is irreversible. Make sure you've exported a backup before proceeding. If browser data was accidentally deleted, recovery is not possible.
